namespace SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioSupport23

def sampleMaximum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s

def sampledFeasible {ι : Type*} (s : ι → ℝ) : Set ℝ := {x | ∀ i, s i ≤ x}

/-- Removing this constraint genuinely permits a smaller objective value. -/
def supporting {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, (∀ j, j ≠ i → s j ≤ x) ∧ x < sampleMaximum s

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) (sampleMaximum s) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact Finset.le_sup' s (Finset.mem_univ i)
  · intro x hx
    exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun i _ => hx i)

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_unique
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (x : ℝ)
    (hx : IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) x) : x = sampleMaximum s :=
  hx.unique (actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum s)

theorem actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ i, sampleMaximum s = s i := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨i, _, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s
  exact ⟨i, hi⟩

Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))=6.9078/0.051293=134.7$, so $N=135$. With one variable only one sample can support the solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)=5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)=115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}=0.911$: so Hoeffding certifies a confidence of only $1-0.911\approx9\%$, not $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).

def feasible {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  {x | x ∈ domain ∧ ∀ i, x ∈ constraints i}

/-- Removing one actual sampled constraint permits a strictly smaller scalar objective. -/
def supportsAt {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum : ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, x ∈ domain ∧ (∀ j, j ≠ i → x ∈ constraints j) ∧ x < optimum

theorem actual_two_distinct_convex_scalar_constraints_cannot_both_support
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hi : supportsAt domain constraints optimum i)
    (hj : supportsAt domain constraints optimum j) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, hxd, hx, hxo⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨y, hyd, hy, hyo⟩ := hj
  rcases le_total x y with hxy | hyx
  · have hcy : y ∈ constraints j :=
      (hc j).ordConnected.out (hx j (Ne.symm hij)) (hopt.1.2 j) ⟨hxy, hyo.le⟩
    have hf : y ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hyd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hkj : k = j
      · exact hkj ▸ hcy
      · exact hy k hkj
    exact (not_le_of_gt hyo) (hopt.2 hf)
  · have hcx : x ∈ constraints i :=
      (hc i).ordConnected.out (hy i hij) (hopt.1.2 i) ⟨hyx, hxo.le⟩
    have hf : x ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hxd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hki : k = i
      · exact hki ▸ hcx
      · exact hx k hki
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxo) (hopt.2 hf)

theorem actual_general_convex_scalar_support_set_has_at_most_one_element
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum) :
    Set.Subsingleton {i | supportsAt domain constraints optimum i} := by
  intro i hi j hj
  by_contra hij
  exact actual_two_distinct_convex_scalar_constraints_cannot_both_support
    domain constraints optimum hc hopt i j hij hi hj

theorem actual_finite_convex_scalar_support_count_is_at_most_one
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum : ℝ) (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    [DecidablePred (supportsAt domain constraints optimum)] :
    (Finset.univ.filter (supportsAt domain constraints optimum)).card ≤ 1 := by
  apply Finset.card_le_one.mpr
  intro i hi j hj
  exact actual_general_convex_scalar_support_set_has_at_most_one_element
    domain constraints optimum hc hopt (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2

end SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioConvexSupport23

import SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedCoverageContinuousTransform
import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsExponentialLesson

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioContinuousRisk23

def sampleMaximum (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (s : Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s

def violation (law : Measure ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ := law.real (Ioi x)

theorem actual_lower_bound_scalar_program_has_unique_attained_optimizer
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (s : Fin n → ℝ) :
    IsLeast {x : ℝ | ∀ i, s i ≤ x} (sampleMaximum n s) ∧
      ∀ x, IsLeast {x : ℝ | ∀ i, s i ≤ x} x → x=sampleMaximum n s := by
  classical
  have h : IsLeast {x : ℝ | ∀ i, s i ≤ x} (sampleMaximum n s) := by
    constructor
    · intro i
      exact Finset.le_sup' s (Finset.mem_univ i)
    · intro x hx
      exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun i _=>hx i)
  exact ⟨h,fun x hx=>hx.unique h⟩

theorem actual_fresh_constraint_violation_is_one_minus_its_cdf
    (law : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law] (x : ℝ) :
    violation law x=1-cdf law x := by
  rw [violation,show Ioi x=(Iic x)ᶜ by ext y;simp,
    probReal_compl_eq_one_sub measurableSet_Iic,←cdf_eq_real law x]

theorem actual_monotone_cdf_commutes_with_the_scalar_optimizer
    (law : Measure ℝ) (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (s : Fin n → ℝ) :
    cdf law (sampleMaximum n s)=sampleMaximum n (fun i=>cdf law (s i)) := by
  classical
  unfold sampleMaximum
  exact Finset.apply_sup'_eq_sup'_comp Finset.univ_nonempty (cdf law)
    (fun x y=>(monotone_cdf law).map_sup x y)

theorem actual_optimized_violation_event_is_all_cdf_coordinates_below_threshold
    {Ω : Type*} (law : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law]
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (epsilon : ℝ) :
    {w | epsilon<violation law (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>X i w))}=
      ⋂ i, {w | cdf law (X i w)<1-epsilon} := by
  classical
  ext w
  rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq,actual_fresh_constraint_violation_is_one_minus_its_cdf,
    actual_monotone_cdf_commutes_with_the_scalar_optimizer]
  have he : epsilon<1-sampleMaximum n (fun i=>cdf law (X i w)) ↔
      sampleMaximum n (fun i=>cdf law (X i w))<1-epsilon := by constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith
  rw [he]
  simp only [sampleMaximum,Finset.sup'_lt_iff,Set.mem_iInter,Set.mem_setOf_eq,
    Finset.mem_univ,forall_const]

theorem actual_iid_continuous_scalar_optimizer_has_exact_violation_tail_probability
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (law : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law] (hc : Continuous (cdf law))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ)
    (hm : ∀ i,Measurable (X i)) (hind : iIndepFun X P)
    (hlaw : ∀ i,HasLaw (X i) law P) (epsilon : ℝ)
    (he : epsilon∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1) :
    P.real {w | epsilon<violation law (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>X i w))}=
      (1-epsilon)^n := by
  let Y : Fin n → Ω → ℝ := fun i w=>cdf law (X i w)
  have hpit:=CompleteAppliedCoverageContinuousTransform.actual_continuous_cdf_probability_integral_transform_has_the_true_uniform_law law hc
  have hi : iIndepFun Y P:=hind.comp (fun _=>cdf law) (fun _=>hc.measurable)
  have hl : ∀ i,HasLaw (Y i) (CompleteAppliedUniformDefinitions.actualUniformLaw 0 1) P:=
    fun i=>hpit.comp (hlaw i)
  have ht : 1-epsilon∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1 := by constructor <;> linarith [he.1,he.2]
  have hp : ∀ i,P.real {w | Y i w<1-epsilon}=1-epsilon := by
    intro i
    exact ((hl i).measureReal_eq measurableSet_Iio).trans
      (CompleteAppliedCoverageUniformLaw.actual_unit_uniform_strict_cdf (1-epsilon) ht)
  have hprod := hi.meas_iInter (s:=fun i=>{w | Y i w<1-epsilon})
    (fun i=>measurableSet_Iio.preimage (comap_measurable (Y i)))
  have hr:=congrArg ENNReal.toReal hprod
  simp only [ENNReal.toReal_prod] at hr
  change P.real (⋂ i,{w | Y i w<1-epsilon})=_ at hr
  simp_rw [←measureReal_def,hp] at hr
  rw [actual_optimized_violation_event_is_all_cdf_coordinates_below_threshold]
  simpa only [Y,Finset.prod_const,Finset.card_univ,Fintype.card_fin] using hr

theorem actual_continuous_scalar_scenario_budget_bounds_the_optimized_risk_event
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (law : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure law] (hc : Continuous (cdf law))
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ)
    (hm : ∀ i,Measurable (X i)) (hind : iIndepFun X P)
    (hlaw : ∀ i,HasLaw (X i) law P) (epsilon beta : ℝ)
    (he : epsilon∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1) (hb : (1-epsilon)^n≤beta) :
    P.real {w | epsilon<violation law (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>X i w))}≤beta ∧
      P.real {w | epsilon<violation law (sampleMaximum n (fun i=>X i w))}≤
        Real.exp (-epsilon*n) := by
  rw [actual_iid_continuous_scalar_optimizer_has_exact_violation_tail_probability
    P law hc n X hm hind hlaw epsilon he]
  exact ⟨hb,CompleteFoundationsExponentialLesson.actual_independent_miss_probability_expression_has_exponential_upper_bound
    epsilon he.1 he.2 n⟩

Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))=6.9078/0.051293=134.7$, so $N=135$. With one variable only one sample can support the solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)=5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)=115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}=0.911$: so Hoeffding certifies a confidence of only $1-0.911\approx9\%$, not $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).
            (d) With probability at least $0.99$ over the validation samples, the posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior.

import SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedDiscountedHorizons
import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsExponentialNumerics
import SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedBinomialModel
import SafeLearning.CompleteAppliedValidation

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000
set_option maxRecDepth 10000
set_option exponentiation.threshold 2000
noncomputable section
open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioNumbers23

def binomialMass (n i : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (n.choose i : ℝ) * p ^ i * (1 - p) ^ (n - i)

def lowerTail (n d : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range d, binomialMass n i p

private theorem mass_successor (n i : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ n) :
    binomialMass (n+1) (i+1) p =
      (1-p)*binomialMass n (i+1) p + p*binomialMass n i p := by
  have he : n-i = (n-(i+1))+1 := by omega
  have he' : n+1-(i+1) = n-i := by omega
  simp only [binomialMass, Nat.choose_succ_succ', Nat.cast_add, he', he, pow_succ]
  ring

private theorem tail_successor_split (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hm : m ≤ n) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p =
      (1-p)*lowerTail n (m+1) p + p*lowerTail n m p := by
  induction m with
  | zero => simp [lowerTail, binomialMass, pow_succ]; ring
  | succ m ih =>
    have hmn : m ≤ n := by omega
    have hs := mass_successor n m p (by omega)
    simp only [lowerTail, Finset.sum_range_succ] at ih ⊢
    have hh := ih hmn
    rw [hs]
    linarith

theorem actual_binomial_tail_successor_identity (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hm : m ≤ n) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p =
      lowerTail n (m+1) p - p*binomialMass n m p := by
  rw [tail_successor_split n m p hm]
  have he : lowerTail n (m+1) p = lowerTail n m p + binomialMass n m p := by
    simp [lowerTail, Finset.sum_range_succ]
  rw [he]
  ring

theorem actual_binomial_tail_nonincrease (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ)
    (hm : m ≤ n) (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p ≤ lowerTail n (m+1) p := by
  rw [actual_binomial_tail_successor_identity n m p hm]
  have hn : 0 ≤ p*binomialMass n m p := by
    unfold binomialMass
    positivity
  linarith

theorem actual_ten_term_tail_antitone_from_nine :
    Antitone (fun k : ℕ => lowerTail (k+9) 10 (1/20)) := by
  apply antitone_nat_of_succ_le
  intro k
  convert actual_binomial_tail_nonincrease (k+9) 9 (1/20) (by omega)
    (by norm_num) (by norm_num) using 1

theorem actual_dimension_one_reduction (n : ℕ) (p : ℝ) :
    lowerTail n 1 p = (1-p)^n := by simp [lowerTail,binomialMass]

theorem actual_independent_count_lower_tail_probability
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n d : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Set Ω) (hA : ∀ i,MeasurableSet (A i))
    (hind : iIndepSet A P) (p : ℝ) (hp : ∀ i,P.real (A i)=p) :
    P.real {w | CompleteAppliedFailureCounts.failureCount A w < d}=lowerTail n d p := by
  classical
  have he : {w | CompleteAppliedFailureCounts.failureCount A w < d}=
      ⋃ i∈Finset.range d,{w | CompleteAppliedFailureCounts.failureCount A w=i} := by
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq,Set.mem_iUnion,Finset.mem_range]
    constructor
    · intro h;exact ⟨_,h,rfl⟩
    · rintro ⟨i,hi,he⟩;omega
  have hd : Set.PairwiseDisjoint (Finset.range d : Set ℕ)
      (fun i=>{w | CompleteAppliedFailureCounts.failureCount A w=i}) := by
    intro i hi j hj hij
    apply Set.disjoint_left.mpr
    intro w hwi hwj
    exact hij (hwi.symm.trans hwj)
  rw [he,measureReal_biUnion_finset hd
    (fun i _ => (measurableSet_singleton i).preimage
      (CompleteAppliedBinomialModel.failure_count_measurable A hA))]
  unfold lowerTail
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  exact CompleteAppliedBinomialModel.actual_binomial_count_mass P n A hA hind p hp i

theorem actual_one_dimensional_boundary_and_rounding :
    (1/1000:ℝ)<(19/20)^134 ∧ (19/20:ℝ)^135<1/1000 ∧
      |Real.log 1000/Real.log (20/19)-1347/10|<1/20 := by
  obtain ⟨hl,hu,_,_⟩ :=
    CompleteAppliedDiscountedHorizons.actual_discount_log_enclosure_and_log_hundred_enclosure
  obtain ⟨_,_,h100l,h100u⟩ :=
    CompleteAppliedDiscountedHorizons.actual_discount_log_enclosure_and_log_hundred_enclosure
  have he1000 : Real.log 1000=(3/2:ℝ)*Real.log 100 := by
    have he : Real.log 1000=3*Real.log 10 := by
      rw [show (1000:ℝ)=(10:ℝ)^3 by norm_num,Real.log_pow]; norm_num
    have he' : Real.log 100=2*Real.log 10 := by
      rw [show (100:ℝ)=(10:ℝ)^2 by norm_num,Real.log_pow]; norm_num
    linarith
  have h1000l : (6907754/1000000:ℝ)<Real.log 1000 := by rw [he1000]; linarith
  have h1000u : Real.log 1000<(6907756/1000000:ℝ) := by rw [he1000]; linarith
  have hd : 0<Real.log (20/19:ℝ) := by linarith
  refine ⟨by norm_num,by norm_num,?_⟩
  rw [abs_lt]
  constructor
  · have h := (lt_div_iff₀ hd).mpr
      (show (1347/10-1/20)*Real.log (20/19)<Real.log 1000 by linarith)
    linarith
  · have h := (div_lt_iff₀ hd).mpr
      (show Real.log 1000<(1347/10+1/20)*Real.log (20/19) by linarith)
    linarith

theorem actual_least_one_dimensional_sample_size (n : ℕ) :
    lowerTail n 1 (1/20) ≤ 1/1000 ↔ 135 ≤ n := by
  rw [actual_dimension_one_reduction]
  norm_num only [show (1-(1/20:ℝ))=19/20 by norm_num]
  constructor
  · intro h
    by_contra hh
    have hn : n ≤ 134 := by omega
    have hm := pow_le_pow_of_le_one (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)≤19/20)
      (by norm_num : (19/20:ℝ)≤1) hn
    exact not_le_of_gt actual_one_dimensional_boundary_and_rounding.1 (hm.trans h)
  · intro hn
    exact (pow_le_pow_of_le_one (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)≤19/20)
      (by norm_num : (19/20:ℝ)≤1) hn).trans
      actual_one_dimensional_boundary_and_rounding.2.1.le

theorem actual_one_dimensional_logarithmic_threshold (n : ℕ) :
    lowerTail n 1 (1/20) ≤ 1/1000 ↔
      Real.log 1000/Real.log (20/19) ≤ (n:ℝ) := by
  rw [actual_dimension_one_reduction]
  have hd : 0<Real.log (20/19:ℝ) := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)
  have hi : Real.log (1-(1/20:ℝ))= -Real.log (20/19) := by
    rw [show (1-(1/20:ℝ))=(20/19)⁻¹ by norm_num,Real.log_inv]
  have hb : Real.log (1/1000:ℝ)= -Real.log 1000 := by
    rw [show (1/1000:ℝ)=(1000:ℝ)⁻¹ by norm_num,Real.log_inv]
  rw [←Real.log_le_log_iff (pow_pos (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)<1-1/20) n)
    (by norm_num),Real.log_pow,hi,hb,div_le_iff₀ hd]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith

theorem actual_ten_variable_boundary_enclosures :
    (10030776/10^12:ℝ)<lowerTail 580 10 (1/20) ∧
      lowerTail 580 10 (1/20)<10030778/10^12 ∧
      (9672779/10^12:ℝ)<lowerTail 581 10 (1/20) ∧

def empirical {Ω : Type*} (n : ℕ) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (w : Ω) : ℝ :=
  (1/(n:ℝ))*∑ i,X i w

private theorem bounded_average_upper_tail
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0<n) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (m epsilon : ℝ)
    (he : 0≤epsilon) (hInd : iIndepFun X P)
    (hm : ∀ i,AEMeasurable (X i) P)
    (hb : ∀ i,∀ᵐ w ∂P,X i w∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1)
    (hmean : ∀ i,∫ w,X i w ∂P = m) :
    P.real {w | epsilon≤empirical n X w-m}≤Real.exp (-2*(n:ℝ)*epsilon^2) := by
  let Y : Fin n → Ω → ℝ := fun i w=>X i w-m
  have hi : iIndepFun Y P := hInd.comp (fun (_:Fin n) (x:ℝ)=>x-m)
    (fun _=>measurable_id.sub_const m)
  have hsg : ∀i,HasSubgaussianMGF (Y i) (1/4) P := by
    intro i
    have h := CompleteAppliedConcentration.centered_unit_interval_subgaussian P (X i) (hm i) (hb i)
    simpa only [hmean i] using h
  have hs : HasSubgaussianMGF (fun w=>∑i,Y i w) ((n:ℝ≥0)/4) P := by
    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using HasSubgaussianMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun hi
      (s:=Finset.univ) (c:=fun _=>(1/4:ℝ≥0)) (fun i _=>hsg i)
  have hnreal : (0:ℝ)<n := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have ht := hs.measure_ge_le (mul_nonneg hnreal.le he)
  have hset : {w | epsilon≤empirical n X w-m}=
      {w | (n:ℝ)*epsilon≤∑i,Y i w} := by
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    have heq : empirical n X w-m=(1/(n:ℝ))*∑i,Y i w := by
      simp only [empirical,Y,Finset.sum_sub_distrib,Finset.sum_const,Finset.card_univ,
        Fintype.card_fin,nsmul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
    rw [heq,one_div_mul_eq_div,le_div_iff₀ hnreal,mul_comm epsilon (n:ℝ)]
  have hexp : -((n:ℝ)*epsilon)^2/(2*((((n:ℝ≥0)/4):ℝ≥0):ℝ))=
      -2*(n:ℝ)*epsilon^2 := by
    push_cast
    field_simp
    ring
  rw [hexp] at ht
  rw [hset]
  exact ht

theorem actual_corrected_validation_samples_certify_the_population_lower_mean
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 5757≤n) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (m : ℝ)
    (hInd : iIndepFun X P) (hm : ∀i,Measurable (X i))
    (hb : ∀i,∀ᵐ w ∂P,X i w∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1)
    (hmean : ∀i,∫w,X i w ∂P = m) :
    (99/100:ℝ)≤P.real {w | empirical n X w-1/50≤ m} := by
  have ht := bounded_average_upper_tail P n (by omega) X m (1/50) (by norm_num)
    hInd (fun i=>(hm i).aemeasurable) hb hmean
  have he : Real.exp (-2*(n:ℝ)*(1/50)^2)≤1/100 := by
    obtain ⟨_,_,hl,hu⟩ :=
      CompleteAppliedDiscountedHorizons.actual_discount_log_enclosure_and_log_hundred_enclosure
    have hnreal : (5757:ℝ)≤n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hlog : Real.log 100≤2*(n:ℝ)*(1/50)^2 := by linarith
    rw [show (1/100:ℝ)=Real.exp (-Real.log 100) by
      rw [Real.exp_neg,Real.exp_log (by norm_num)];norm_num,Real.exp_le_exp]
    linarith
  have hbadMeas : MeasurableSet {w | m<empirical n X w-1/50} :=
    measurableSet_lt measurable_const
      ((measurable_const.mul (Finset.measurable_sum Finset.univ (fun i _=>hm i))).sub_const _)
  have hbad : P.real {w | m<empirical n X w-1/50}≤1/100 := by
    apply (measureReal_mono (μ:=P) (show {w | m<empirical n X w-1/50}⊆
      {w | (1/50:ℝ)≤empirical n X w-m} by intro w hw;dsimp at hw ⊢;linarith)).trans
    exact ht.trans he
  have hc := probReal_compl_eq_one_sub (μ:=P) hbadMeas
  have hset : {w | m<empirical n X w-1/50}ᶜ={w | empirical n X w-1/50≤ m} := by
    ext w;simp
  rw [hset] at hc
  linarith

theorem actual_accepted_fixed_validation_certifies_point_nine_three
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 5757≤n) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (m : ℝ)
    (hInd : iIndepFun X P) (hm : ∀i,Measurable (X i))
    (hb : ∀i,∀ᵐ w ∂P,X i w∈Icc (0:ℝ) 1)
    (hmean : ∀i,∫w,X i w ∂P = m) :
    (99/100:ℝ)≤P.real {w | (19/20≤empirical n X w)→93/100≤ m} := by
  have h := actual_corrected_validation_samples_certify_the_population_lower_mean
    P n hn X m hInd hm hb hmean
  exact h.trans (measureReal_mono (μ:=P) (by
    intro w hw hh;change empirical n X w-1/50≤ m at hw;linarith))

theorem actual_normalized_credible_region_transfers_stability_to_full_belief
    {Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Θ] (posterior : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure posterior]
    (credible stable : Set Θ) (hc : posterior.real credible=19/20)
    (hm : (93/100:ℝ)≤posterior.real (credible∩stable)/posterior.real credible) :
    (1767/2000:ℝ)≤posterior.real stable ∧ (22/25:ℝ)≤posterior.real stable := by
  have hm' : (1767/2000:ℝ)≤posterior.real (credible∩stable) := by
    rw [hc,le_div_iff₀ (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)<19/20)] at hm
    nlinarith
  have hs := measureReal_mono (μ:=posterior) (inter_subset_right : credible∩stable⊆stable)
  constructor
  · exact hm'.trans hs
  · linarith [hm'.trans hs]

theorem actual_independent_normalized_posterior_validation_has_point_eight_eight_confidence
    {Ω Θ : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Θ]
    (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (posterior : Measure Θ) [IsProbabilityMeasure posterior]
    (credible stable : Set Θ) (hc : posterior.real credible=19/20)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 5757≤n) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (p : unitInterval)
    (hp : (p:ℝ)=posterior.real (credible∩stable)/posterior.real credible)
    (hInd : iIndepFun X P) (hm : ∀i,Measurable (X i))
    (hLaw : ∀i,HasLaw (X i) (bernoulliMeasure (1:ℝ) 0 p) P) :
    (99/100:ℝ)≤P.real {w | (19/20≤empirical n X w)→22/25≤posterior.real stable} := by
  have hs := actual_accepted_fixed_validation_certifies_point_nine_three
    P n hn X p hInd hm
    (fun i=>(CompleteAppliedValidation.bernoulli_support_mean P (X i) p (hLaw i)).1)
    (fun i=>(CompleteAppliedValidation.bernoulli_support_mean P (X i) p (hLaw i)).2)
  exact hs.trans (measureReal_mono (μ:=P) (by
    intro w hw hh
    have hpop := hw hh
    rw [hp] at hpop
    exact (actual_normalized_credible_region_transfers_stability_to_full_belief
      posterior credible stable hc hpop).2))

theorem actual_source_logarithm_roundings_and_strict_numerical_inequalities :
    |Real.log 1000-69078/10000|<1/20000 ∧
      |Real.log (20/19)-51293/1000000|<1/2000000 ∧
      Real.log 1000/Real.log (20/19)<1347/10 ∧
      Real.log 1000≠69078/10000 ∧
      Real.log (20/19)≠51293/1000000 ∧
      Real.log 1000/Real.log (20/19)≠1347/10 := by
  obtain ⟨hl,hu,h100l,h100u⟩ :=
    CompleteAppliedDiscountedHorizons.actual_discount_log_enclosure_and_log_hundred_enclosure
  have hlog : Real.log 1000=(3/2:ℝ)*Real.log 100 := by
    have h1 : Real.log 1000=3*Real.log 10 := by
      rw [show (1000:ℝ)=10^3 by norm_num,Real.log_pow];norm_num
    have h2 : Real.log 100=2*Real.log 10 := by
      rw [show (100:ℝ)=10^2 by norm_num,Real.log_pow];norm_num
    linarith
  have hd : 0<Real.log (20/19:ℝ) := by linarith
  have hr : Real.log 1000/Real.log (20/19)<1347/10 := by
    apply (div_lt_iff₀ hd).mpr
    rw [hlog]
    linarith
  refine ⟨?_,?_,hr,?_,?_,ne_of_lt hr⟩
  · rw [hlog,abs_lt];constructor <;> linarith
  · rw [abs_lt];constructor <;> linarith
  · rw [hlog];intro h;linarith
  · intro h;linarith

import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsIndependentTrials

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false

open Set MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioSupport23

def sampleMaximum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s

def sampledFeasible {ι : Type*} (s : ι → ℝ) : Set ℝ := {x | ∀ i, s i ≤ x}

/-- Removing this constraint genuinely permits a smaller objective value. -/
def supporting {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, (∀ j, j ≠ i → s j ≤ x) ∧ x < sampleMaximum s

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) (sampleMaximum s) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact Finset.le_sup' s (Finset.mem_univ i)
  · intro x hx
    exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun i _ => hx i)

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_unique
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (x : ℝ)
    (hx : IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) x) : x = sampleMaximum s :=
  hx.unique (actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum s)

theorem actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ i, sampleMaximum s = s i := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨i, _, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s
  exact ⟨i, hi⟩

theorem actual_support_constraint_is_a_strict_unique_maximum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hi : supporting s i) : sampleMaximum s = s i ∧ ∀ j, j ≠ i → s j < s i := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, hxm⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample s
  have hki : k = i := by
    by_contra h
    have hle := hx k h
    rw [← hk] at hle
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxm) hle
  have he : sampleMaximum s = s i := hki ▸ hk
  refine ⟨he, ?_⟩
  intro j hj
  have hl := hx j hj
  rw [he] at hxm
  exact hl.trans_lt hxm

theorem actual_strict_unique_maximum_is_a_support_constraint
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hi : ∀ j, j ≠ i → s j < s i) : supporting s i := by
  classical
  have hm : sampleMaximum s = s i := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun j _ => by
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · exact hji ▸ le_rfl
        · exact (hi j hji).le)

import Mathlib

set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
noncomputable section
open Set

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioConvexSupport23

def feasible {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  {x | x ∈ domain ∧ ∀ i, x ∈ constraints i}

/-- Removing one actual sampled constraint permits a strictly smaller scalar objective. -/
def supportsAt {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum : ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, x ∈ domain ∧ (∀ j, j ≠ i → x ∈ constraints j) ∧ x < optimum

theorem actual_two_distinct_convex_scalar_constraints_cannot_both_support
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hi : supportsAt domain constraints optimum i)
    (hj : supportsAt domain constraints optimum j) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, hxd, hx, hxo⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨y, hyd, hy, hyo⟩ := hj
  rcases le_total x y with hxy | hyx
  · have hcy : y ∈ constraints j :=
      (hc j).ordConnected.out (hx j (Ne.symm hij)) (hopt.1.2 j) ⟨hxy, hyo.le⟩
    have hf : y ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hyd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hkj : k = j
      · exact hkj ▸ hcy
      · exact hy k hkj
    exact (not_le_of_gt hyo) (hopt.2 hf)
  · have hcx : x ∈ constraints i :=
      (hc i).ordConnected.out (hy i hij) (hopt.1.2 i) ⟨hyx, hxo.le⟩
    have hf : x ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hxd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hki : k = i
      · exact hki ▸ hcx
      · exact hx k hki
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxo) (hopt.2 hf)

theorem actual_general_convex_scalar_support_set_has_at_most_one_element
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum) :
    Set.Subsingleton {i | supportsAt domain constraints optimum i} := by
  intro i hi j hj
  by_contra hij
  exact actual_two_distinct_convex_scalar_constraints_cannot_both_support
    domain constraints optimum hc hopt i j hij hi hj

theorem actual_finite_convex_scalar_support_count_is_at_most_one
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum : ℝ) (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    [DecidablePred (supportsAt domain constraints optimum)] :
    (Finset.univ.filter (supportsAt domain constraints optimum)).card ≤ 1 := by
  apply Finset.card_le_one.mpr
  intro i hi j hj
  exact actual_general_convex_scalar_support_set_has_at_most_one_element
    domain constraints optimum hc hopt (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2

end SafeLearning.CompleteLyapunovScenarioConvexSupport23

def binomialMass (n i : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (n.choose i : ℝ) * p ^ i * (1 - p) ^ (n - i)

def lowerTail (n d : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ Finset.range d, binomialMass n i p

private theorem mass_successor (n i : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ n) :
    binomialMass (n+1) (i+1) p =
      (1-p)*binomialMass n (i+1) p + p*binomialMass n i p := by
  have he : n-i = (n-(i+1))+1 := by omega
  have he' : n+1-(i+1) = n-i := by omega
  simp only [binomialMass, Nat.choose_succ_succ', Nat.cast_add, he', he, pow_succ]
  ring

private theorem tail_successor_split (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hm : m ≤ n) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p =
      (1-p)*lowerTail n (m+1) p + p*lowerTail n m p := by
  induction m with
  | zero => simp [lowerTail, binomialMass, pow_succ]; ring
  | succ m ih =>
    have hmn : m ≤ n := by omega
    have hs := mass_successor n m p (by omega)
    simp only [lowerTail, Finset.sum_range_succ] at ih ⊢
    have hh := ih hmn
    rw [hs]
    linarith

theorem actual_binomial_tail_successor_identity (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ) (hm : m ≤ n) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p =
      lowerTail n (m+1) p - p*binomialMass n m p := by
  rw [tail_successor_split n m p hm]
  have he : lowerTail n (m+1) p = lowerTail n m p + binomialMass n m p := by
    simp [lowerTail, Finset.sum_range_succ]
  rw [he]
  ring

theorem actual_binomial_tail_nonincrease (n m : ℕ) (p : ℝ)
    (hm : m ≤ n) (hp : 0 ≤ p) (hp1 : p ≤ 1) :
    lowerTail (n+1) (m+1) p ≤ lowerTail n (m+1) p := by
  rw [actual_binomial_tail_successor_identity n m p hm]

private theorem bounded_average_upper_tail
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0<n) (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (m epsilon : ℝ)
    (he : 0≤epsilon) (hInd : iIndepFun X P)
    (hm : ∀ i,AEMeasurable (X i) P)

    P.real {w | epsilon≤empirical n X w-m}≤Real.exp (-2*(n:ℝ)*epsilon^2) := by

    simpa only [hmean i] using h

    simpa [div_eq_mul_inv] using HasSubgaussianMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun hi
      (s:=Finset.univ) (c:=fun _=>(1/4:ℝ≥0)) (fun i _=>hsg i)

      simp only [empirical,Y,Finset.sum_sub_distrib,Finset.sum_const,Finset.card_univ,

def sampleMaximum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s

def sampledFeasible {ι : Type*} (s : ι → ℝ) : Set ℝ := {x | ∀ i, s i ≤ x}

/-- Removing this constraint genuinely permits a smaller objective value. -/
def supporting {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, (∀ j, j ≠ i → s j ≤ x) ∧ x < sampleMaximum s

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) (sampleMaximum s) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro i
    exact Finset.le_sup' s (Finset.mem_univ i)
  · intro x hx
    exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun i _ => hx i)

theorem actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_unique
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (x : ℝ)
    (hx : IsLeast (sampledFeasible s) x) : x = sampleMaximum s :=
  hx.unique (actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum s)

theorem actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    ∃ i, sampleMaximum s = s i := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨i, _, hi⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_sup' Finset.univ_nonempty s
  exact ⟨i, hi⟩

theorem actual_support_constraint_is_a_strict_unique_maximum
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hi : supporting s i) : sampleMaximum s = s i ∧ ∀ j, j ≠ i → s j < s i := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx, hxm⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := actual_sample_maximum_is_attained_by_a_sample s
  have hki : k = i := by
    by_contra h
    have hle := hx k h
    rw [← hk] at hle
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxm) hle
  have he : sampleMaximum s = s i := hki ▸ hk
  refine ⟨he, ?_⟩
  intro j hj
  have hl := hx j hj
  rw [he] at hxm
  exact hl.trans_lt hxm

theorem actual_strict_unique_maximum_is_a_support_constraint
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) (i : ι)
    (hi : ∀ j, j ≠ i → s j < s i) : supporting s i := by
  classical
  have hm : sampleMaximum s = s i := by
    apply le_antisymm
    · exact (Finset.sup'_le_iff Finset.univ_nonempty s).mpr (fun j _ => by
        by_cases hji : j = i
        · exact hji ▸ le_rfl
        · exact (hi j hji).le)
    · exact (actual_scalar_scenario_optimizer_is_the_sample_maximum s).1 i
  by_cases he : (Finset.univ.erase i : Finset ι).Nonempty
  · refine ⟨(Finset.univ.erase i).sup' he s, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro j hj
      exact Finset.le_sup' s (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hj, Finset.mem_univ j⟩)
    · rw [hm]
      exact (Finset.sup'_lt_iff he).mpr (fun j hj => hi j (Finset.mem_erase.mp hj).1)
  · refine ⟨s i - 1, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro j hj
      exact False.elim (he ⟨j, Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hj, Finset.mem_univ j⟩⟩)
    · rw [hm]
      linarith

theorem actual_at_most_one_sample_constraint_is_supporting
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ) :
    Set.Subsingleton {i | supporting s i} := by
  intro i hi j hj
  by_contra hij
  have hji := (actual_support_constraint_is_a_strict_unique_maximum s i hi).2 j (Ne.symm hij)
  have hij' := (actual_support_constraint_is_a_strict_unique_maximum s j hj).2 i hij
  exact (not_lt_of_ge hij'.le) hji

theorem actual_support_sample_count_is_at_most_one
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (s : ι → ℝ)
    [DecidablePred (supporting s)] :
    (Finset.univ.filter (supporting s)).card ≤ 1 := by
  apply Finset.card_le_one.mpr
  intro i hi j hj
  exact actual_at_most_one_sample_constraint_is_supporting s
    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2 (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2

theorem actual_sample_maximum_threshold_event_is_exactly_all_misses
    {Ω ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Nonempty ι] (X : ι → Ω → ℝ) (q : ℝ) :
    {w | sampleMaximum (fun i => X i w) ≤ q} = ⋂ i, {w | q < X i w}ᶜ := by
  classical
  ext w
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_iInter, Set.mem_compl_iff, not_lt,
    sampleMaximum, Finset.sup'_le_iff, Finset.mem_univ, forall_const]

theorem actual_independent_scalar_scenario_threshold_failure_probability
    {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
    (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (X : Fin n → Ω → ℝ) (q epsilon : ℝ)
    (hX : ∀ i, MeasurableSet {w | q < X i w})
    (hind : iIndepSet (fun i => {w | q < X i w}) P)
    (he : ∀ i, P.real {w | q < X i w} = epsilon)
    (hepsilon : epsilon ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) :
    P.real {w | sampleMaximum (fun i => X i w) ≤ q} = (1-epsilon)^n ∧
      P.real {w | sampleMaximum (fun i => X i w) ≤ q} ≤ Real.exp (-epsilon*n) := by
  rw [actual_sample_maximum_threshold_event_is_exactly_all_misses X q]
  exact CompleteFoundationsIndependentTrials.actual_independent_events_have_the_true_all_miss_probability_and_exponential_bound
    P n (fun i => {w | q < X i w}) epsilon hX hind hepsilon he

Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))=6.9078/0.051293=134.7$, so $N=135$. With one variable only one sample can support the solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)=5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)=115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}=0.911$: so Hoeffding certifies a confidence of only $1-0.911\approx9\%$, not $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).
            (d) With probability at least $0.99$ over the validation samples, the posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior.

def feasible {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) : Set ℝ :=
  {x | x ∈ domain ∧ ∀ i, x ∈ constraints i}

/-- Removing one actual sampled constraint permits a strictly smaller scalar objective. -/
def supportsAt {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ)
    (optimum : ℝ) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ, x ∈ domain ∧ (∀ j, j ≠ i → x ∈ constraints j) ∧ x < optimum

theorem actual_two_distinct_convex_scalar_constraints_cannot_both_support
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum)
    (i j : ι) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hi : supportsAt domain constraints optimum i)
    (hj : supportsAt domain constraints optimum j) : False := by
  obtain ⟨x, hxd, hx, hxo⟩ := hi
  obtain ⟨y, hyd, hy, hyo⟩ := hj
  rcases le_total x y with hxy | hyx
  · have hcy : y ∈ constraints j :=
      (hc j).ordConnected.out (hx j (Ne.symm hij)) (hopt.1.2 j) ⟨hxy, hyo.le⟩
    have hf : y ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hyd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hkj : k = j
      · exact hkj ▸ hcy
      · exact hy k hkj
    exact (not_le_of_gt hyo) (hopt.2 hf)
  · have hcx : x ∈ constraints i :=
      (hc i).ordConnected.out (hy i hij) (hopt.1.2 i) ⟨hyx, hxo.le⟩
    have hf : x ∈ feasible domain constraints := by
      refine ⟨hxd, ?_⟩
      intro k
      by_cases hki : k = i
      · exact hki ▸ hcx
      · exact hx k hki
    exact (not_le_of_gt hxo) (hopt.2 hf)

theorem actual_general_convex_scalar_support_set_has_at_most_one_element
    {ι : Type*} (domain : Set ℝ) (constraints : ι → Set ℝ) (optimum : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, Convex ℝ (constraints i))
    (hopt : IsLeast (feasible domain constraints) optimum) :
    Set.Subsingleton {i | supportsAt domain constraints optimum i} := by
  intro i hi j hj
  by_contra hij

exact_whole_exercise_literal.source_text:
Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))=6.9078/0.051293=134.7$, so $N=135$. With one variable only one sample can support the solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)=5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)=115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}=0.911$: so Hoeffding certifies a confidence of only $1-0.911\approx9\%$, not $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).
            (d) With probability at least $0.99$ over the validation samples, the posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior.

entire_inventory_record.label: Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
entire_inventory_record.source_text:
Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically
      
      
        (a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))$. For the given values, $\ln1000/\ln(20/19)\approx134.7$ (with $\ln1000\approx6.9078$ and $\ln(20/19)\approx0.051293$), so $N=135$. Under the convex scenario-program assumptions, at most one sample can support the one-variable solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.
            (b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.
            (c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)\approx5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)\approx115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}\approx0.911$. Hoeffding supplies the lower confidence bound $1-e^{-0.0928}\approx9\%$, rather than $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).
            (d) For a fixed $K^\ast$ and one fresh independent batch of at least $5757$ validation samples from the normalized $c=0.95$ credible posterior, with probability at least $0.99$ over that batch, acceptance (empirical stability at least $0.95$) implies that the full posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior. This is a fixed-batch implication; repeated validation attempts need a separate failure budget.

Hertneck et al. (2018): robustness by design, validation by Hoeffding

Hertneck, Köhler, Trimpe & Allgöwer, L-CSS 2018 make the MPC tolerate the error it will later suffer: treat $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}(x)=\pi_{\mathrm{MPC}}(x)+d$, $\|d\|_\infty\le\eta$, as an input disturbance. The robust MPC is a nominal MPC with terminal set $X_f$ and tightened constraints $\bar X_k=(1-\epsilon_k)X$, $\bar U_k=(1-\epsilon_k)U_t$, $U_t=U\ominus\{\|d\|_\infty\le\eta\}$, $\epsilon_k=\epsilon(1-\sqrt\rho^{\,k})/(1-\sqrt\rho)$ growing like a tube. Assumptions 1–4: local incremental stabilisability (a $\delta$-Lyapunov function contracting at rate $\rho\lt1$), $\|f(x,u+d)-f(x,u)\|\le\lambda\|d\|_\infty$, a bound on $\eta$, and a robustly invariant terminal set with a local control Lyapunov function. Written out:

Definition — The robust-design assumptions of Hertneck et al. (2018, Assumptions 1–4 and eq. 9)
Assumption 1 (local incremental stabilisability). There are a feedback $\kappa(x,z,v)$, a $\delta$-Lyapunov function $V_\delta(x,z,v)\ge0$ with $V_\delta(z,z,v)=0$, and constants $c_{\delta,l},c_{\delta,u},\delta_{\rm loc},k_{\max}\gt0$, $\rho\in(0,1)$ such that, whenever $V_\delta(x,z,v)\le\delta_{\rm loc}$, $$c_{\delta,l}\|x-z\|^2\le V_\delta(x,z,v)\le c_{\delta,u}\|x-z\|^2,\qquad\|\kappa(x,z,v)-v\|\le k_{\max}\|x-z\|,\qquad V_\delta(x^+,z^+,v^+)\le\rho\,V_\delta(x,z,v),$$ with $x^+=f(x,\kappa(x,z,v))$ and $z^+=f(z,v)$: a feedback that lets the true state $x$ track a nominal trajectory $z$ driven by inputs $v$, the squared tracking error shrinking by the factor $\rho$ per step.
Assumption 2. $\|f(x,u+d)-f(x,u)\|\le\lambda\|d\|_\infty$ for $x\in X$ and $u,\,u+d\in U$.
Assumption 3. $\eta\le\lambda^{-1}\sqrt{\delta_{\rm loc}/c_{\delta,u}}$.
Tightening (eq. 9). With $X=\{x:Hx\le\mathbf 1\}$ and $U_t=\{u:L_tu\le\mathbf 1\}$: $\epsilon:=\eta\lambda\sqrt{c_{\delta,u}/c_{\delta,l}}\,\max\{\|H\|_\infty,\|L_t\|_\infty k_{\max}\}$ and $\epsilon_k=\epsilon\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\sqrt\rho^{\,j}$.
Assumption 4 (terminal set). $V_f(x)=x^\top Px$, $X_f=\{V_f\le\alpha_f\}$ and a controller $k_f$ with, for all $x\in X_f$: $f(x,k_f(x))+w\in X_f$ for every $\|w\|\le\lambda\eta\sqrt{\rho^Nc_{\delta,u}/c_{\delta,l}}$; $V_f(f(x,k_f(x)))\le V_f(x)-\big(x^\top Qx+k_f(x)^\top Rk_f(x)\big)$; $(x,k_f(x))\in\bar X_N\times\bar U_N$.
In words. An input error $\|d\|_\infty\le\eta$ moves the next state by at most $\lambda\eta$ (Assumption 2), so the re-planned trajectory starts within $V_\delta\le c_{\delta,u}\lambda^2\eta^2\le\delta_{\rm loc}$ of the old plan: Assumption 3 is exactly what keeps this inside the region where the tracking certificate holds. Afterwards $\sqrt{V_\delta}$ shrinks by $\sqrt\rho$ per step, so $k$ steps later the state is within $\sqrt\rho^{\,k}\lambda\eta\sqrt{c_{\delta,u}/c_{\delta,l}}$ of the old plan; in constraint units (factors $\|H\|_\infty$, and $\|L_t\|_\infty k_{\max}$ for inputs) this is at most $\epsilon\sqrt\rho^{\,k}=\epsilon_{k+1}-\epsilon_k$, the increment of the tightening. What is left after $N$ steps is the ball the terminal set must absorb. All of this is checked before learning; validation only estimates how often the network stays within $\eta$.
Theorem — Robust MPC and its learned approximation (Hertneck et al. 2018, Theorems 5 and 8)
Theorem 5. Under Assumptions 1–4, from every $x(0)\in X_{\mathrm{feas}}$ the closed loop with inputs $\pi_{\mathrm{MPC}}(x)+d$, $\|d\|_\infty\le\eta$, satisfies $(x(t),u(t))\in X_{\mathrm{feas}}\times U$ for all $t$ and converges to a robust positively invariant set around the origin. So any $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ with $\|\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}-\pi_{\mathrm{MPC}}\|_\infty\le\eta$ on the visited states inherits this.
Validation. Draw initial conditions i.i.d. from $\Omega$ on $X_{\mathrm{feas}}$, simulate $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ until $X_f$, and set $I(X_i)=1$ if the error bound held along the whole trajectory. From $X_f$ on, the terminal controller $k_f$ of Assumption 4 takes over: the validated trajectories end in $X_f$, "where we can guarantee stability and constraint satisfaction with the terminal controller" (their Sec. IV-B and Remark 6), and $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ is never checked inside $X_f$. With $\mu=\mathbb P[I=1]$ and the empirical mean $\tilde\mu$ of $p$ runs, Hoeffding (their Lemma 7) gives $\mathbb P[|\tilde\mu-\mu|\ge\epsilon_h]\le2e^{-2p\epsilon_h^2}=:\delta_h$; the test passes if $$\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}\ \le\ \tilde\mu-\sqrt{\ln(2/\delta_h)/(2p)} .$$ Theorem 8. If validation succeeds, then with confidence at least $1-\delta_h$ the approximate MPC ensures stability and constraint satisfaction for a fraction $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$ of the initial conditions distributed according to $\Omega$. This holds for the hybrid controller that switches to $k_f$ on entering $X_f$; keeping $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ inside $X_f$ would need a separate guarantee there.
In words. Robustness makes an error bound sufficient; statistics estimates how often it holds. The guarantee concerns a random initial condition, not every initial condition.
Validation protocol. A run counts as a success only if it reaches $X_f$ and the error bound held at every step before; in finite computation, fix a maximal horizon and count non-entry by then as failure (conservative). Freeze the controller before drawing each validation batch: after retraining, or when the sample is enlarged until the test passes, use a fresh batch with a split confidence budget (step 6 below) or a time-uniform bound.
Derivation — The Hoeffding sample bound for validating an approximate MPC

1. Random variables. The indicators $I(X_1),\dots,I(X_p)$ are i.i.d. (i.i.d. initial conditions, deterministic closed loop), with values in $[0,1]$ and mean $\mu$.

2. Hoeffding. For i.i.d. variables in $[a,b]$, $\mathbb P[\tilde\mu-\mu\ge\epsilon]\le e^{-2p\epsilon^2/(b-a)^2}$ and likewise for the lower tail; for $[0,1]$ and both tails, $\mathbb P[|\tilde\mu-\mu|\ge\epsilon_h]\le2e^{-2p\epsilon_h^2}$.

3. Margin. Setting this to $\delta_h$ gives $\epsilon_h=\sqrt{\ln(2/\delta_h)/(2p)}$: with probability at least $1-\delta_h$ over the validation data, $\mu\ge\tilde\mu-\epsilon_h$. Only the lower tail matters, so the one-sided $\sqrt{\ln(1/\delta_h)/(2p)}$ would do; the paper uses the two-sided one.

4. Sample size. With an expected success rate $\tilde\mu\gt\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$ the test passes once $\epsilon_h\le\tilde\mu-\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$: $$p\ \ge\ \frac{\ln(2/\delta_h)}{2(\tilde\mu-\mu_{\mathrm{crit}})^2},$$ which explodes as $\tilde\mu\downarrow\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$: certifying $99\%$ needs an approximator visibly better than $99\%$.

5. The paper's example. A stirred-tank reactor, horizon $N=180$, $\eta=5.1\cdot10^{-3}$, $\delta_h=0.01$, $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}=0.99$: validation passed with $\tilde\mu=0.9987$ on $p=34\,980$ trajectories. Here $\epsilon_h=\sqrt{\ln200/69\,960}=0.00870$, so at most 45 failures are allowed. The whole procedure took roughly 500 hours on a quad-core PC.

6. Two probability levels, one subtlety. $\delta_h$ refers to the validation sample, $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$ to a fresh initial condition, and the confidence to one validation run of one fixed controller. If the test is repeated (more samples, or retraining) until it passes, as the algorithm allows, a union bound over at most $K$ attempts (see Primer C) at level $\delta_h/K$ each restores confidence $1-\delta_h$.

7. Statistical Guarantees Meet Robust Control (Fiedler, Scherer, Trimpe)

Robust control certifies a controller for every member of an uncertainty set; learning produces sets that are correct only with high probability. Composing the two gives closed-loop guarantees with the probability of the learning step, provided the learned set is expressed in the language of robust control. Three statistical tools recur.

Definition — Hoeffding's inequality and sub-Gaussianity
For i.i.d. $Z_1,\dots,Z_p\in[a,b]$ with mean $\mu$ and $\bar Z=\frac1p\sum_iZ_i$: $\ \mathbb P[\bar Z-\mu\ge t]\le\exp\big(-2pt^2/(b-a)^2\big)$, and twice that for $|\bar Z-\mu|$. For indicators, $\mu\ge\bar Z-t$ at confidence $1-\delta$ needs $p\ge\ln(1/\delta)/(2t^2)$. The proof rests on Hoeffding's lemma: a variable in $[a,b]$ is $\tfrac{b-a}2$-sub-Gaussian, the noise model of the GP bounds in Module 3. Use: a-posteriori validation of a fixed design.
Theorem — The scenario approach (Calafiore & Campi 2006; exact bound of Campi & Garatti 2008)
Setting. A convex program with $d$ decision variables and uncertain convex constraints $\theta\in\Theta_\delta$, $\delta\sim P$ (in this box $\delta$ is the uncertain parameter, as in the scenario literature, not a failure probability; $\theta$ is the decision variable, not a policy parameter). Solve the scenario program $\min c^\top\theta$ s.t. $\theta\in\Theta_{\delta^{(i)}}$ for $N$ i.i.d. samples; its solution $\theta_N^\ast$ is assumed to exist and be unique (possibly via a tie-break rule). Violation probability: $V(\theta)=P\{\delta:\theta\notin\Theta_\delta\}$.
Statement. For any $P$ (binomial tails: Primer C), $$P^N\big\{V(\theta_N^\ast)\gt\epsilon\big\}\ \le\ \sum_{i=0}^{d-1}\binom Ni\epsilon^i(1-\epsilon)^{N-i},$$ with equality for fully-supported problems (Campi & Garatti, SIAM J. Optim. 2008), sharpening the earlier $\binom Nd(1-\epsilon)^{N-d}$ (Calafiore & Campi, TAC 2006, their eq. 11, from which their explicit sample-size formulas are derived). A simple sufficient size, which follows from a Chernoff bound on the binomial tail and is the form von Rohr et al. use (after Campi, Garatti & Prandini, Annu. Rev. Control 2009), is $N\ge\frac2\epsilon(\ln\frac1\beta+d)$.
In words. At most $d$ sampled constraints support the solution, so violating more than an $\epsilon$-fraction has binomial-tail probability. Use: a-priori design of convex (e.g. LMI) controllers. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$, $d=10$: exact $N=581$, older bound 1344, sufficient formula 861 (our computation).
Reading the statement. A support constraint is a sampled constraint whose removal changes the solution; convexity allows at most $d$ of them. Fully supported means that, with probability one, the solution has exactly $d$ of them; only the equality case needs this. There are two probability levels: $V(\theta)$ is the probability that one fresh uncertain system violates the design, while $P^N\{V(\theta_N^\ast)\gt\epsilon\}$ is the probability, over the $N$ design samples, of drawing a sample that produces a design with $V\gt\epsilon$. The sample-size calculator below applies only to feasible convex scenario programs with the solution assumptions above.

The third tool is the uniform GP error bound of Module 3: a tube $|\varphi(x)-\mu_D(x)|\le\beta_D\sigma_D(x)$ for all $x$ simultaneously, with probability $1-\delta$ over the data, for a fixed unknown function. This frequentist reading is what robust control needs.

Fiedler, Scherer & Trimpe (CDC 2021): from a GP tube to IQC synthesis

Fiedler, Scherer & Trimpe, CDC 2021 build a pipeline in which every stage carries a guarantee. The plant is a linear fractional representation: a known LTI part $G$ in feedback with $p=\Delta(q)$, here a diagonal static nonlinearity $p_i=\varphi_i(q_i)$, $i\le n_p$, whose unknown parts are "pulled out" so that all prior knowledge stays in $G$.

Background — Linear fractional representations and the star product

A linear fractional representation (LFR) separates a known linear system from an uncertain block. With an external input $w$ (e.g. a disturbance) and a performance output $z$, the known part is $q=G_{qp}p+G_{qw}w$, $z=G_{zp}p+G_{zw}w$, and the loop is closed by $p=\Delta(q)$. If $\Delta$ is a matrix and $I-G_{qp}\Delta$ is invertible, eliminating $p$ and $q$ gives

$$z=\Big(G_{zw}+G_{zp}\Delta\big(I-G_{qp}\Delta\big)^{-1}G_{qw}\Big)w,$$

and this closed map is written $\Delta\star G$ (the star product; below, $\Delta_0\star P$). Well-posedness means that the loop equations have a unique solution for every $w$; for a matrix $\Delta$ it is the invertibility of $I-G_{qp}\Delta$. Example: scalar $G_{qp}=\tfrac12$, $\Delta=1$ gives $q=\tfrac q2+G_{qw}w$, so $q=2G_{qw}w$; with $G_{qp}=\Delta=1$ the equation $q=q+G_{qw}w$ has no solution unless $G_{qw}w=0$, an ill-posed loop, which must be excluded before any stability claim.

  1. Learn. $y_n=\varphi(x_n)+\epsilon_n$ with independent $R$-sub-Gaussian noise (Assumption 1), $\varphi\in\mathcal H_k$, $\|\varphi\|_k\le B$ (Assumption 2); prior knowledge such as $\varphi(0)=0$ goes into the kernel, $k_0(x,x')=k(x,x')-k(x,0)k(x',0)/k(0,0)$ (for $k(0,0)\gt0$). This is the covariance of a zero-mean GP conditioned on the exact observation $\varphi(0)=0$ (Gaussian conditioning, Primer C), so $k_0(0,x)=0$ and every sample vanishes at $0$; in the frequentist reading used here, $\mathcal H_{k_0}$ consists exactly of the functions in $\mathcal H_k$ with $\varphi(0)=0$, with the same norm, so Assumption 2 carries over.
  2. Bound. Proposition 1: $\mathbb P[|\varphi(x)-\mu_D(x)|\le\beta_D\sigma_D(x)\ \forall x]\ge1-\delta$ with a data-dependent $\beta_D$.
  3. Sector. $\varphi$ is in the sector $[\kappa_1,\kappa_2]$ if $\kappa_1x^2\le x\varphi(x)\le\kappa_2x^2$ (Module 2). Lemma 2 gives the tightest sector compatible with the tube on $[a,b]$: $\hat\kappa_1=\inf_{x\in[a,b]\setminus\{0\}}\min\{x(\mu_D-\beta_D\sigma_D),\,x(\mu_D+\beta_D\sigma_D)\}/x^2$ and $\hat\kappa_2$ likewise with outer supremum and inner maximum, so with probability $1-\delta$ the true $\varphi$ lies in the sector $[\hat\kappa_1,\hat\kappa_2]$ on $[a,b]$: $\hat\kappa_1x^2\le x\varphi(x)\le\hat\kappa_2x^2$ there. Equivalently, $[\kappa_1,\kappa_2]\subseteq[\hat\kappa_1,\hat\kappa_2]$ for the tightest local sector, $\kappa_1=\inf_{[a,b]\setminus\{0\}}\varphi(x)/x$ and $\kappa_2$ likewise with sup. The paper states the containment for any sector of $\varphi$, which fails for a loose one: $\varphi(x)=x$ lies in $[-10,10]$, but an exact tube gives $[1,1]$. (For $x\ne0$ the tube gives an interval for $\varphi(x)/x$; dividing by a negative $x$ swaps its endpoints, hence the inner $\min$/$\max$. The punctured interval is not compact, hence $\inf$/$\sup$, and the ratios can blow up near $0$: the sector is finite only if, e.g., $|\mu_D(x)|+\beta_D\sigma_D(x)\le C|x|$ near $0$.)
  4. Multipliers. With $\hat\kappa_1^{(i)}\le0\le\hat\kappa_2^{(i)}$ (Assumption 3), full-block multipliers on the vertices of the estimated sector box cover all channels; step 2 with $\delta/n_p$ per channel and a union bound makes the IQC description valid with probability $1-\delta$ (Lemma 3).
  5. Synthesise. IQC analysis LMIs (via the KYP lemma, Module 2) alternate with controller synthesis until the robust performance level $\tilde\gamma$ stops improving (later use for neural networks: Module 14).
Going deeper — Why vertex conditions give a valid multiplier

Write the diagonal nonlinearity as $p=\Theta q$ with $\Theta=\mathrm{diag}(\theta_i)$ and $\theta_i=\varphi_i(q_i)/q_i\in[\hat\kappa_1^{(i)},\hat\kappa_2^{(i)}]$ (any value in the interval if $q_i=0$). A symmetric $\Pi$ is a valid static multiplier if $[q;p]^\top\Pi[q;p]\ge0$ for all such pairs. The full-block class of Fiedler et al. (their eq. 18) requires

$$\Pi_{pp}:=\begin{bmatrix}0\\I\end{bmatrix}^\top\Pi\begin{bmatrix}0\\I\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,\qquad\begin{bmatrix}I\\\Theta\end{bmatrix}^\top\Pi\begin{bmatrix}I\\\Theta\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\ \ \text{at every vertex }\theta_i\in\{\hat\kappa_1^{(i)},\hat\kappa_2^{(i)}\}.$$

This suffices: for fixed $q$, $\theta\mapsto[q;\Theta q]^\top\Pi[q;\Theta q]$ is quadratic in $\theta$ with second-order part $(\Theta q)^\top\Pi_{pp}(\Theta q)\le0$, hence concave, and a concave function on a box takes its minimum at a vertex, where it is nonnegative. With probability at least $1-\delta$ every true $\varphi_i$ lies in its estimated sector (Lemma 3), and on that event any controller certified for the whole class (well-posedness, stability, and a performance level such as $\|z\|_{L_2}\le\tilde\gamma\|w\|_{L_2}$ from zero initial state) is certified for the true plant. Because the sectors are learned on $[a_i,b_i]$ only, the loop signals must also be shown to stay there (caveat below).

Theorem — Learning-enhanced robust synthesis (Fiedler, Scherer & Trimpe 2021, Theorem 1)
Assumptions. Assumptions 1–3; learning per channel with $\delta/n_p$; multipliers as in Lemma 3 (full-block, vertex conditions above); the synthesis certifies well-posedness, stability and the performance level for the whole sector class and returns $K$ after $M\ge1$ iterations with robust performance level $\tilde\gamma_{M+1}$. Since the sectors are learned on $[a_i,b_i]$ only, the loop signals must stay in these intervals (our addition; the paper omits the details, see the caveat).
Statement. With probability at least $1-\delta$, $K$ stabilises the true system and achieves robust performance level $\tilde\gamma_{M+1}$.
In words. The ground truth lies in the learned set with probability $1-\delta$ and the robust guarantee covers the whole set; more data shrink the set and improve performance.
Caveat — reading the CDC 2021 result correctly
  • The constant. Proposition 1 prints $\beta_D=B+2R\sqrt{\log\det(K_D+\bar\lambda I_N)-2\log\delta}$, $\bar\lambda=\max\{1,\lambda\}$: a pre-correction form. Like the AAAI 2021 print version (which has $R$ where this has $2R$) it lacks the factor $1/\sqrt\lambda$ and the $\bar\lambda/\lambda$ inside the determinant that the correction added. For $\lambda\ge1$ it dominates the corrected bound and stays valid, only conservative; for $\lambda\lt1$ use the corrected Theorem 1 of Module 3.
  • Local sectors. The sector is computed on $[a,b]$ but used as a global condition; the loop signals must be shown to stay in $[a,b]$ (the paper says this can be done with robust-control techniques and omits details), or the certificate is local.
  • Known $B$ and frequentist reading. The RKHS-norm bound must be given (Module 5). The authors contrast their setting with randomised robust control such as the scenario approach: there probability refers to the algorithm's samples, here only the data are random and the ground truth is fixed.

Exploration with a-priori robustness. Holicki, Scherer & Trimpe, L-CSS 2021 take the complementary route for a partially unknown linear plant $P_0=\Delta_0\star P$, $\Delta_0\in\boldsymbol\Delta$ known. They partition $\boldsymbol\Delta=\bigcup_k\boldsymbol\Delta_k$ and, for each partition member, synthesise by IQC/LMI relaxation (their Theorem 1) a controller $F(k)$ that robustly stabilises all of $\boldsymbol\Delta$ while optimising the worst-case performance over $\boldsymbol\Delta_k$ only. Every controller of the family therefore stabilises every plant in $\boldsymbol\Delta$, so experiments can explore the index with any black-box method without risk of instability. The paper separates two gaps. Refining the partition around the best member shrinks the parameterisation gap, their (P). The "cost of safety", their gap (S), comes from demanding stabilisation of all of $\boldsymbol\Delta$, and a finer partition of the same set leaves it unchanged. It shrinks only when the members inconsistent with the measurements, those whose measured cost $L(k)$ of $F(k)$ exceeds the level $\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$ that Theorem 1 certifies for $F(k)$ over $\boldsymbol\Delta_k$, are discarded (their eq. 13, since $\Delta_0\in\boldsymbol\Delta_k$ implies $L(k)\le\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$) and the family is redesigned for the smaller remaining set. It is the robust-control answer to safe BO (Module 4): certify candidates a priori, not statistically.

Fact — Safe experiments and sound elimination in the controller family (Holicki et al. 2021)
Assumptions. The true plant is $\Delta_0\star P$ with $\Delta_0\in\boldsymbol\Delta=\bigcup_k\boldsymbol\Delta_k$; for each tested index $k$ the synthesis certifies that $F(k)$ well-posedly stabilises $\Delta\star P$ for every $\Delta\in\boldsymbol\Delta$ and that $\|\Delta\star P\star F(k)\|_\infty\le\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$ for every $\Delta\in\boldsymbol\Delta_k$; the measured cost is the same quantity, $L(k)=\|\Delta_0\star P\star F(k)\|_\infty$, or a valid lower bound on it.
Statement. Every experiment with a fixed $F(k)$ is stable. If $L(k)\gt\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$, then $\Delta_0\notin\boldsymbol\Delta_k$ (otherwise the certificate would give $L(k)\le\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$), so discarding such members never discards the true plant. With a measurement error $|L_{\rm measured}(k)-L(k)|\le e_k$, discard only if $L_{\rm measured}(k)-e_k\gt\gamma_\varepsilon^\ast(k)$.
Scope. The certificates cover each controller used on its own; switching between controllers during one experiment is not covered, and a redesign for the remaining set must again certify all of it.

Probabilistic robust LQR with GPs (von Rohr et al. 2021)

von Rohr, Neumann-Brosig & Trimpe, L4DC 2021 differentiate a GP dynamics model at the operating point, obtaining a Bayesian (matrix-normal) posterior over $S=[\bar A\ \bar B]$, truncated to its credible region of mass $c$ (a region of posterior probability $c$; Primer C). With $\phi_K=\mathbb 1[\rho(\bar A+\bar BK)\lt1]$ they seek $\mathbb E[\phi_K]\ge1-\epsilon$ at minimal expected LQR cost. A priori: the initial controller solves a common-Lyapunov LMI over $M$ sampled systems, a convex scenario program with $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables; their Theorem 1 gives $\mathbb E[\phi_{K_{\mathrm{init}}}]\ge1-\epsilon$ with probability greater than $1-\beta$ if $M\ge\lceil\frac2\epsilon(\ln\frac1\beta+n_k)\rceil$. A posteriori: the improvement steps (a majorise–minimise scheme averaging over samples; see the MM background in Section 3) are not a scenario program, so the final $K^\ast$ is returned only if its empirical stability rate on $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ fresh samples satisfies $\hat\phi\ge1-\epsilon$.

Background — Derivatives of a GP, matrix-normal posteriors and the common-Lyapunov LMI

Derivatives of a GP. If the mean $m_a$ and covariance $k_{ab}(z,z')$ of a vector-valued GP have continuous mixed second derivatives near the operating point, difference quotients are linear combinations of jointly Gaussian values, and their mean-square limits, the partial derivatives, are again jointly Gaussian with mean $\partial_im_a(z)$ and covariance

$$\operatorname{Cov}\big(\partial_if_a(z),\partial_jf_b(z')\big)=\partial_{z_i}\partial_{z'_j}k_{ab}(z,z').$$

Conditioning on data with Gaussian noise (Primer C) gives a Gaussian posterior over these derivatives, i.e. over the entries of $S=[\bar A\ \bar B]$. Matrix-normal is a special, separable structure: $\operatorname{vec}(S)\sim\mathcal N(\operatorname{vec}(M),C\otimes R)$, with $R$ the covariance between rows, $C$ between columns, and $C\otimes R$ the block matrix with blocks $C_{ij}R$; general derivative posteriors need not have it. Either way this is uncertainty about a local linearisation, not a nonlinear stability certificate.

The common-Lyapunov LMI. For sampled systems $(A_i,B_i)$ look for $X\succ0$ and $Y$ with

$$\begin{bmatrix}X&(A_iX+B_iY)^\top\\A_iX+B_iY&X\end{bmatrix}\succ0\quad\text{for every }i,\qquad K:=YX^{-1}.$$

With $Y=KX$ the off-diagonal block is $(A_i+B_iK)X$; the Schur complement (Module 2) turns the LMI into $X-X(A_i+B_iK)^\top X^{-1}(A_i+B_iK)X\succ0$, and multiplying by $X^{-1}$ on both sides gives $(A_i+B_iK)^\top P(A_i+B_iK)-P\prec0$ with $P=X^{-1}$: one Lyapunov matrix for all sampled systems. The conditions are linear in $(X,Y)$, so this is a convex scenario program; its $n_k$ must count all scalar decision variables, including any performance variables.

Caveat — corrected statement of the validation theorem (von Rohr et al. 2021, Theorem 2)
Theorem 2 prints $M_{\mathrm{val}}\ge\frac1{2\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}}\log\frac1\alpha$, but its proof uses $\mathbb P(\hat\phi-\mathbb E\phi\ge\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})\le e^{-2M_{\mathrm{val}}\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}^2}$, which is at most $\alpha$ only if $$M_{\mathrm{val}}\ \ge\ \frac{\log(1/\alpha)}{2\,\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}^2}:$$ for $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, 5757 samples instead of the printed 116. Eq. (8) prints $\mathbb P(\mathbb E[\phi_{K^\ast}]\ge1-\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}})\gt1-\alpha$ with $\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}}=c-(\epsilon+\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})$, whereas the proof concludes $\mathbb P(\mathbb E[\phi]\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{pr}})\le\alpha$. Consistent statement: with probability at least $1-\alpha$ over the validation samples, the posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $c-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$, since Hoeffding gives $\mathbb E_{P_c}[\phi]\ge1-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$ on the truncated posterior and truncation removes mass $1-c$: $\mathbb E_P[\phi]\ge c(1-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}})\ge c-\epsilon-\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}$. Both slips are visible in the full text (statement versus proof); arXiv v2 fixes a different typo in Algorithm 1. This guarantee is Bayesian, unlike Fiedler et al.'s, and the algorithm repeats until the test passes, so the union-bound remark of Section 6 applies.

Exercise 11.3 — Validating an approximate MPC with Hoeffding

Take $\delta_h=0.01$, $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}=0.99$ as in Hertneck et al. (a) Your network violates the error bound on about $0.2\%$ of trajectories ($\tilde\mu\approx0.998$). How many validation trajectories are needed with the two-sided bound, and with the one-sided one? (b) With the paper's $p=34\,980$, how many failures can the test tolerate? (c) You may retrain and re-validate up to $K=5$ times, using fresh independent IID validation trajectories for each trained controller: which per-attempt confidence keeps the overall one at $0.99$, and what happens to $p$ in (a)? (d) State precisely what a passed test guarantees.

Show answer

(a) Need $\epsilon_h\le0.998-0.99=0.008$. Two-sided: $p\ge\ln200/(2\cdot0.008^2)=\ln200/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx41\,393.1$, so $41\,394$. One-sided: $\ln100/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx35\,977.9$, so $35\,978$.

(b) $\epsilon_h=\sqrt{\ln200/(2\cdot34\,980)}\approx0.0087025$, so the exact test requires $\tilde\mu\ge0.99+\epsilon_h\approx0.9987025$, i.e. at least $34\,935$ successes: at most 45 failures. (The reported $0.9987$ is rounded; exactly $0.9987$ would fail by about $3\cdot10^{-6}$.)

(c) Union bound: $0.01/5=0.002$ per attempt, so $p\ge\ln(1000)/(1.28\cdot10^{-4})\approx53\,966.8$, i.e. $53\,967$ (two-sided): about 30% more samples buy honesty about repeated testing.

(d) With probability at least $1-\delta_h$ over the validation data, a fresh initial condition from the same $\Omega$ gives a trajectory with $\|\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}-\pi_{\mathrm{MPC}}\|_\infty\le\eta$ with probability at least $\mu_{\mathrm{crit}}$ until it enters $X_f$; on it Theorem 5 gives constraint satisfaction up to that entry, after which the terminal controller $k_f$ keeps the state in $X_f$ and gives convergence (Remark 6). The guarantee is for this switched controller: $\pi_{\mathrm{approx}}$ itself is not validated inside $X_f$. Nothing is said for other initial distributions.

Exercise 11.4 — Scenario design and validation, numerically

(a) For $d=1$ show that the Campi–Garatti bound reduces to $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta$; compute $N$ for $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-3}$. (b) A common-Lyapunov LMI with $d_x=2$, $d_u=1$ has $n_k=2d_x^2+d_xd_u$ variables. For $\epsilon=0.05$, $\beta=10^{-5}$ compare the exact scenario sample size (calculator) with the sufficient formula. (c) For validation with $\alpha=0.01$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{val}}=0.02$, compute $M_{\mathrm{val}}$ with the corrected and the misprinted rule; what confidence does the misprinted size give? (d) With $c=0.95$, $\epsilon=0.05$ and (c), what does the corrected theorem guarantee?

Show answer

(a) Only the term $i=0$ remains: $(1-\epsilon)^N\le\beta\iff N\ge\ln(1/\beta)/(-\ln(1-\epsilon))$. For the given values, $\ln1000/\ln(20/19)\approx134.7$ (with $\ln1000\approx6.9078$ and $\ln(20/19)\approx0.051293$), so $N=135$. Under the convex scenario-program assumptions, at most one sample can support the one-variable solution, and a violation above $\epsilon$ needs all $N$ samples to miss an $\epsilon$-mass region.

(b) $n_k=10$. The binomial tail first drops below $10^{-5}$ at $N=581$ ($9.67\cdot10^{-6}$; at $580$ it is $1.003\cdot10^{-5}$); the sufficient formula gives $\lceil40(\ln10^5+10)\rceil=861$, about 48% more.

(c) Corrected: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02^2)\approx5756.5$, so $5757$. Misprinted: $\ln100/(2\cdot0.02)\approx115.1$, so $116$, for which $e^{-2\cdot116\cdot0.02^2}=e^{-0.0928}\approx0.911$. Hoeffding supplies the lower confidence bound $1-e^{-0.0928}\approx9\%$, rather than $99\%$ (a lower bound from this inequality, not the actual confidence of the procedure).

(d) For a fixed $K^\ast$ and one fresh independent batch of at least $5757$ validation samples from the normalized $c=0.95$ credible posterior, with probability at least $0.99$ over that batch, acceptance (empirical stability at least $0.95$) implies that the full posterior probability that $K^\ast$ stabilises the true linearisation is at least $0.95-0.05-0.02=0.88$: a Bayesian statement, as good as the GP posterior. This is a fixed-batch implication; repeated validation attempts need a separate failure budget.

/-- A local quadratic upper bound plus continuity rules out leaving the local
Lyapunov sublevel before the end of a sufficiently short line segment. The
bound is assumed only where the Lyapunov value is already local. -/
theorem continuous_local_quadratic_bound_bootstraps_the_endpoint
    (V : ℝ → ℝ) (delta c : ℝ) (hdelta : 0 < delta) (hc : 0 ≤ c)
    (hsmall : c ≤ delta) (hcontinuous : ContinuousOn V (Icc 0 1))
    (hzero : V 0 = 0)
    (hlocal : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 1, V t ≤ delta → V t ≤ c * t ^ 2) :
    V 1 ≤ c := by
  have hendpoint : V 1 ≤ delta := by
    by_contra hnot
    have habove : delta < V 1 := lt_of_not_ge hnot
    obtain ⟨t, ht, heq⟩ := intermediate_value_Ioo (show (0 : ℝ) ≤ 1 by norm_num)
      hcontinuous (show delta ∈ Ioo (V 0) (V 1) by simpa [hzero] using And.intro hdelta habove)
    have hbound := hlocal t ⟨ht.1.le, ht.2.le⟩ (by simpa [heq])
    have hsq : t ^ 2 < 1 := by nlinarith [ht.1, ht.2]
    have hmult : c * t ^ 2 ≤ delta * t ^ 2 :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hsmall (sq_nonneg t)
    have hstrict : delta * t ^ 2 < delta := by nlinarith
    rw [heq] at hbound
    linarith
  simpa using hlocal 1 (by norm_num) hendpoint

end SafeLearning.CompleteCoreMPCLocalBootstrap27

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteCoreMPCLocalBootstrap27

theorem continuous_local_quadratic_state_bound_bootstraps_small_state_error
    {S : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup S] [NormedSpace ℝ S]
    (X : Set S) (hX : Convex ℝ X) (V : S → ℝ) (z x : S)
    (hz : z ∈ X) (hx : x ∈ X) (delta cU : ℝ)
    (hdelta : 0 < delta) (hcU : 0 ≤ cU)
    (hsmall : cU * ‖x - z‖ ^ 2 ≤ delta)
    (hcontinuous : ContinuousOn V X) (hzero : V z = 0)
    (hlocal : ∀ y ∈ X, V y ≤ delta → V y ≤ cU * ‖y - z‖ ^ 2) :
    V x ≤ cU * ‖x - z‖ ^ 2 := by
  let path : ℝ → S := fun t => z + t • (x - z)
  have hpath : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 1, path t ∈ X := by
    intro t ht
    exact hX.add_smul_sub_mem hz hx ht
  have hpcontinuous : Continuous path :=
    continuous_const.add (continuous_id.smul continuous_const)
  have hvcontinuous : ContinuousOn (fun t => V (path t)) (Icc 0 1) :=
    hcontinuous.comp hpcontinuous.continuousOn hpath
  have hpzero : path 0 = z := by simp [path]
  have hpone : path 1 = x := by simp [path]
  have hbound := continuous_local_quadratic_bound_bootstraps_the_endpoint
    (fun t => V (path t)) delta (cU * ‖x - z‖ ^ 2) hdelta
    (mul_nonneg hcU (sq_nonneg _)) hsmall hvcontinuous (by simpa [hpzero] using hzero)
    (by
      intro t ht hvalue
      have hh := hlocal (path t) (hpath t ht) hvalue
      have hpnorm : ‖path t - z‖ = t * ‖x - z‖ := by
        simp only [path, add_sub_cancel_left, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
          abs_of_nonneg ht.1]
      rw [hpnorm] at hh
      convert hh using 1 <;> ring)
  simpa [hpone] using hbound

end SafeLearning.CompleteCoreMPCLocalBootstrap27

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteCoreMPCLocalBootstrap27

def polytopicStateSet {S J : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup S] [NormedSpace ℝ S]
    (rows : J → S →L[ℝ] ℝ) (margin : ℝ) : Set S :=
  {state | ∀ j, rows j state ≤ 1 - margin}

theorem actual_linear_constraint_margin_covers_every_bounded_state_perturbation
    {S J : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup S] [NormedSpace ℝ S]
    (rows : J → S →L[ℝ] ℝ) (z x : S) (H radius margin : ℝ)
    (hH : 0 ≤ H) (hrows : ∀ j, ‖rows j‖ ≤ H)
    (hz : z ∈ polytopicStateSet rows margin)
    (herror : ‖x - z‖ ≤ radius) (hmargin : H * radius ≤ margin) :
    x ∈ polytopicStateSet rows 0 := by
  intro j
  have hlinear : rows j x = rows j z + rows j (x - z) := by
    rw [map_sub]
    ring
  have hnorm := (rows j).le_opNorm (x - z)
  have hrowerror : rows j (x - z) ≤ H * radius := by
    calc
      rows j (x - z) ≤ ‖rows j (x - z)‖ := by
        simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using le_abs_self (rows j (x - z))
      _ ≤ ‖rows j‖ * ‖x - z‖ := hnorm
      _ ≤ H * ‖x - z‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hrows j) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ ≤ H * radius := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left herror hH
  have hnominal := hz j
  rw [hlinear]
  linarith

end SafeLearning.CompleteCoreMPCLocalBootstrap27

    (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) : ‖(fun i => x i)‖ ≤ ‖x‖ := by

theorem actual_matrix_infinity_row_sum_bound_controls_euclidean_state_error
    (H : Matrix J I ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (j : J) :
    |(H *ᵥ (fun i => x i)) j| ≤ ‖H‖ * ‖x‖ := by

    (u v : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) (k error : ℝ) (hbound : ‖u - v‖ ≤ k * error) :
    ‖(fun i => u i - v i)‖ ≤ k * error := by
